rv.q: The latest of them, “A Tale of Two Cities,” is by no means the least, but it’s a lumbering artifact — overwrought, under-nuanced and hopelessly old-fashioned.

This stolid poperetta, which features book, music and lyrics by Jill Santoriello and is directed and choreographed by Warren Carlyle, is one of those unfortunate shows that are neither witty in themselves nor able to inspire wit in others.
The entertaining evening unfortunately lacks inspiration.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this pop opera adaptation, with some praising its gifted voices and handsome design while others find it a lumpish attempt to recreate the magic of Les Misérables.

vs.sum: The Al Hirschfeld Theatre offers generally good sightlines, though some seats have minor obstructions. The sound quality is above average, enhancing the theatrical experience. However, the seating is cramped, especially for taller patrons, which detracts from comfort. The theater's ambiance is rich with historical character, though restroom lines can be long during intermission.

acc.note: Orchestra-only wheelchair access. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops available.
